en: to stand someone up
exampleFr: Il m'a posé un lapin hier soir ; je l'ai attendu au restaurant pendant une heure.
exampleEn: He stood me up last night; I waited for him at the restaurant for an hour.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put down a rabbit' — the odd image has nothing to do with animals; it means failing to show up to an arranged meeting or date.

en: to feel down, to have the blues
exampleFr: Depuis la fin des vacances, j'ai le cafard.
exampleEn: Since the holidays ended, I've been feeling down.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the cockroach' — the creepy insect stands for a gloomy, melancholic mood, not an actual bug.

fr: coûter les yeux de la tête
en: to cost an arm and a leg
lemma: coûter les yeux de la tête
exampleFr: Cette voiture de sport coûte les yeux de la tête.
exampleEn: That sports car costs an arm and a leg.
mnemonic: Literally 'to cost the eyes of the head' — an absurdly high price so extreme it's as if you'd have to give up your own eyes to pay it.
audioText: coûter les yeux de la tête

en: it's raining cats and dogs, pouring rain
exampleFr: Prends ton parapluie, il pleut des cordes dehors !
exampleEn: Take your umbrella, it's pouring outside!
mnemonic: Literally 'it's raining ropes' — the rain is imagined as thick as ropes falling from the sky, meaning it's pouring heavily.

en: to annoy or bore someone
exampleFr: Arrête de me casser les pieds avec tes questions !
exampleEn: Stop bugging me with your questions!
mnemonic: Literally 'to break someone's feet' — no actual injury involved; it means to annoy or pester someone relentlessly.

en: to be daydreaming
exampleFr: Excuse-moi, je n'ai pas écouté, j'étais dans la lune.
exampleEn: Sorry, I wasn't listening, I was daydreaming.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be on the moon' — describing someone so distracted or lost in thought they seem to have floated off to outer space.

fr: prendre ses jambes à son cou
en: to run away as fast as possible
lemma: prendre ses jambes à son cou
exampleFr: Quand il a vu le chien, il a pris ses jambes à son cou.
exampleEn: When he saw the dog, he ran away as fast as he could.
mnemonic: Literally 'to take one's legs to one's neck' — a comic image of legs pumping so hard while fleeing that they seem to reach up to the neck.
audioText: prendre ses jambes à son cou

fr: avoir un chat dans la gorge
en: to have a frog in one's throat
lemma: avoir un chat dans la gorge
exampleFr: Je suis désolée, j'ai un chat dans la gorge, je ne peux plus parler normalement.
exampleEn: Sorry, I have a frog in my throat, I can't speak normally.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a cat in the throat' — no cat is actually stuck there; it just means your voice sounds hoarse or scratchy.
audioText: avoir un chat dans la gorge

fr: mettre les pieds dans le plat
en: to put one's foot in it, to blunder tactlessly
lemma: mettre les pieds dans le plat
exampleFr: Il a encore mis les pieds dans le plat en parlant du divorce devant toute la famille.
exampleEn: He put his foot in it again by bringing up the divorce in front of the whole family.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put one's feet in the serving dish' — like stomping into the food at dinner, it means blurting out something tactless or embarrassing.
audioText: mettre les pieds dans le plat

en: to faint, to pass out
exampleFr: Il faisait si chaud qu'elle est tombée dans les pommes.
exampleEn: It was so hot that she fainted.
mnemonic: Literally 'to fall into the apples' — an odd fruity image with no logical fruit connection; it simply means to lose consciousness.

en: to fall in love at first sight
exampleFr: Quand je l'ai rencontrée, ça a été le coup de foudre immédiat.
exampleEn: When I met her, it was love at first sight.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the bolt of lightning' — falling in love is compared to being struck suddenly and powerfully, just like a lightning bolt.

en: to give up guessing
exampleFr: Je ne trouve pas la réponse, je donne ma langue au chat.
exampleEn: I can't find the answer, I give up.
mnemonic: Literally 'to give one's tongue to the cat' — handing your tongue away means you're giving up trying to answer a riddle or guess something.

en: to feel great, to be full of energy
exampleFr: Ce matin, j'ai la pêche, je suis prêt à tout !
exampleEn: This morning I'm feeling great, I'm ready for anything!
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the peach' — the plump, vibrant fruit represents feeling energetic, healthy, and in great shape.

en: to have a big smile, to be beaming
exampleFr: Depuis qu'il a eu son diplôme, il a la banane toute la journée.
exampleEn: Ever since he got his diploma, he's had a big grin all day.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the banana' — the curved fruit's shape mirrors a wide, curved smile stretching across the face.

en: to be at the end of one's rope, exhausted
exampleFr: Après trois nuits blanches, il était au bout du rouleau.
exampleEn: After three sleepless nights, he was completely worn out.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be at the end of the roll' — like a roll of paper or thread that has completely unwound, meaning someone has no energy left.

fr: mettre la charrue avant les bœufs
en: to put the cart before the horse
lemma: mettre la charrue avant les bœufs
exampleFr: Signer le bail avant d'avoir le travail, c'est mettre la charrue avant les bœufs.
exampleEn: Signing the lease before getting the job is putting the cart before the horse.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put the plough before the oxen' — a farming image of doing things in the wrong order, since oxen must pull the plough, not follow it.
audioText: mettre la charrue avant les bœufs

en: to call a spade a spade
exampleFr: Il faut appeler un chat un chat : ce projet est un échec.
exampleEn: We have to call a spade a spade: this project is a failure.
mnemonic: Literally 'to call a cat a cat' — naming a thing exactly what it is, plainly and honestly, without euphemism.

fr: avoir un poil dans la main
en: to be very lazy
lemma: avoir un poil dans la main
exampleFr: Il n'a rien fait de la journée, il a vraiment un poil dans la main.
exampleEn: He hasn't done anything all day, he's incredibly lazy.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a hair in the hand' — implying the hand is so unused from laziness that a hair has had time to grow right in the palm.
audioText: avoir un poil dans la main

en: to have other fish to fry, other priorities
exampleFr: Je ne peux pas t'aider maintenant, j'ai d'autres chats à fouetter.
exampleEn: I can't help you right now, I have other things to deal with.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have other cats to whip' — a strange old expression meaning you have more urgent matters to attend to than the one at hand.

en: to overcomplicate a simple matter
exampleFr: Ce n'est pas compliqué, arrête de chercher midi à quatorze heures !
exampleEn: It's not complicated, stop overanalyzing everything!
mnemonic: Literally 'to look for noon at two o'clock' — searching for something at the wrong, illogical time reflects making a simple issue needlessly complex.

en: to sleep in
exampleFr: Le dimanche, j'aime faire la grasse matinée jusqu'à midi.
exampleEn: On Sundays, I like to sleep in until noon.
mnemonic: Literally 'to make the fat morning' — a 'plump,' extended morning in bed, i.e., sleeping much later than usual.

fr: avoir la tête dans les nuages
en: to have one's head in the clouds
lemma: avoir la tête dans les nuages
exampleFr: Concentre-toi un peu, tu as toujours la tête dans les nuages !
exampleEn: Focus a little, your head is always in the clouds!
mnemonic: Literally 'to have one's head in the clouds' — the same image as in English: being distracted, unrealistic, or lost in daydreams.
audioText: avoir la tête dans les nuages

en: to throw in the towel, to give up
exampleFr: Après des mois d'échecs, il a fini par jeter l'éponge.
exampleEn: After months of failure, he finally gave up.
mnemonic: Literally 'to throw the sponge' — borrowed from boxing, where throwing the sponge into the ring signals surrender.

en: to fall in love easily, to be fickle-hearted
exampleFr: Elle tombe amoureuse toutes les semaines, elle a vraiment un cœur d'artichaut.
exampleEn: She falls in love every week, she really has a heart that falls for everyone.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have an artichoke heart' — just as an artichoke has many leaves each hiding a bit of heart, this person gives a 'leaf' of their heart to everyone they meet.

en: to tell tall tales, to talk nonsense or lies
exampleFr: Ne l'écoute pas, il raconte toujours des salades.
exampleEn: Don't listen to him, he's always making things up.
mnemonic: Literally 'to tell salads' — a jumbled mix of vegetables mirrors a jumbled, unreliable mix of exaggerations and lies.

fr: avoir la moutarde qui monte au nez
en: to lose one's temper, to start seething
lemma: avoir la moutarde qui monte au nez
ipa: /a.vwaʁ la mu.taʁd ki mɔ̃t o ne/
exampleFr: Quand il a entendu cette insulte, la moutarde lui est montée au nez.
exampleEn: When he heard that insult, he lost his temper.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the mustard rising to the nose' — like the sharp sting mustard gives your nose, sudden anger is described as a rising burn.
audioText: avoir la moutarde qui monte au nez

fr: il n'y a pas le feu au lac
en: there's no rush, no need to hurry
lemma: il n'y a pas le feu au lac
ipa: /il nja pa lə fø o lak/
exampleFr: Détends-toi, il n'y a pas le feu au lac, on a toute la journée.
exampleEn: Relax, there's no rush, we have the whole day.
mnemonic: Literally 'there's no fire at the lake' — since a lake wouldn't burn anyway, the joke underlines that there's truly nothing urgent happening.
audioText: il n'y a pas le feu au lac

en: to be in a real mess, in trouble
exampleFr: Si le patron découvre ça, on va être dans de beaux draps.
exampleEn: If the boss finds out about this, we'll be in serious trouble.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be in beautiful sheets' — used ironically: 'beautiful' sheets are actually a tangled mess you're stuck in, meaning a difficult situation.

en: to have connections, to be influential
exampleFr: Il a obtenu ce poste facilement, son père a le bras long dans cette entreprise.
exampleEn: He got that job easily, his father has a lot of influence in that company.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a long arm' — a long reach lets someone influence things far beyond their immediate grasp, i.e., have powerful connections.

fr: mettre la main à la pâte
en: to pitch in, to get one's hands dirty helping
lemma: mettre la main à la pâte
exampleFr: Pour finir à temps, tout le monde doit mettre la main à la pâte.
exampleEn: To finish on time, everyone needs to pitch in.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put one's hand in the dough' — like a baker kneading dough, it means actively helping with a task rather than just watching.
audioText: mettre la main à la pâte

en: to see stars (after being hit)
exampleFr: Il a reçu le ballon en pleine tête et a vu trente-six chandelles.
exampleEn: He got hit in the head by the ball and saw stars.
mnemonic: Literally 'to see thirty-six candles' — a dazzling number of imaginary lights flashing before your eyes after a hard blow to the head.

en: to beat around the bush
exampleFr: Dis-moi ce qui ne va pas au lieu de tourner autour du pot.
exampleEn: Tell me what's wrong instead of beating around the bush.
mnemonic: Literally 'to turn around the pot' — circling the cooking pot instead of reaching into it mirrors avoiding the real point of a conversation.

en: to be full of oneself, conceited
exampleFr: Depuis son succès, il a un peu la grosse tête.
exampleEn: Since his success, he's gotten a bit full of himself.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the big head' — an inflated head represents an inflated ego, i.e., being arrogant or conceited.

en: to kill two birds with one stone
exampleFr: En allant à la boulangerie, je suis aussi passée à la banque : j'ai fait d'une pierre deux coups.
exampleEn: By going to the bakery, I also stopped at the bank: I killed two birds with one stone.
mnemonic: Literally 'to make two hits with one stone' — one thrown stone achieving two results, meaning to accomplish two goals with a single action.

fr: être sur son trente et un
en: to be dressed to the nines
lemma: être sur son trente et un
exampleFr: Pour le mariage, elle était sur son trente et un.
exampleEn: For the wedding, she was dressed to the nines.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be on one's thirty-one' — an old, mysterious number tied to elegant dress; it means being dressed in one's very best clothes.
audioText: être sur son trente et un

en: to put in one's two cents, to interject unasked
exampleFr: Il faut toujours qu'il mette son grain de sel dans nos conversations.
exampleEn: He always has to put in his two cents during our conversations.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put in one's grain of salt' — a small pinch of seasoning added uninvited, like an unsolicited comment or opinion.

en: to be thriving, to have the wind at one's back
exampleFr: Depuis leur dernier album, ce groupe a le vent en poupe.
exampleEn: Since their latest album, this band has been on a roll.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the wind in the stern' — like a sailboat pushed forward by favorable wind, meaning things are going remarkably well.

en: to leave without saying goodbye, to slip away
exampleFr: La fête était ennuyeuse, alors j'ai filé à l'anglaise.
exampleEn: The party was boring, so I slipped away without saying goodbye.
mnemonic: Literally 'to leave English style' — an old French dig at English manners, meaning to depart quietly without formal farewells.

en: it's all over, that's the last straw
exampleFr: Si on rate ce train, c'est la fin des haricots pour nos vacances.
exampleEn: If we miss this train, that's the end of our vacation plans.
mnemonic: Literally 'it's the end of the beans' — when even the cheapest, last food (beans) runs out, it means the situation has hit rock bottom.

en: to be extremely ambitious, greedy for success
exampleFr: Ce jeune cadre a les dents longues, il veut la direction générale avant trente ans.
exampleEn: That young executive is fiercely ambitious, he wants to be CEO before he's thirty.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have long teeth' — like a predator with oversized teeth ready to bite into every opportunity, showing intense ambition or greed.

fr: mettre du beurre dans les épinards
en: to improve one's financial situation a little
lemma: mettre du beurre dans les épinards
exampleFr: Ce petit boulot du week-end met du beurre dans les épinards.
exampleEn: This little weekend job brings in some extra money.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put butter in the spinach' — adding a rich touch to a plain dish represents adding a bit of extra comfort to modest finances.
audioText: mettre du beurre dans les épinards

en: to be ravenously hungry
exampleFr: Après le match, les enfants avaient une faim de loup.
exampleEn: After the game, the kids were ravenously hungry.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a wolf's hunger' — a wolf is a fierce hunter, so this hunger is imagined as fierce and insatiable.

fr: être pris la main dans le sac
en: to be caught red-handed
lemma: être pris la main dans le sac
ipa: /ɛtʁ pʁi la mɛ̃ dɑ̃ lə sak/
exampleFr: Le voleur a été pris la main dans le sac par la police.
exampleEn: The thief was caught red-handed by the police.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be caught with the hand in the bag' — a thief literally caught with a hand still inside the stolen bag, i.e., caught in the act.
audioText: être pris la main dans le sac

en: to have a hitch, a minor problem
exampleFr: Désolé pour le retard, j'ai eu un petit pépin avec ma voiture.
exampleEn: Sorry for being late, I had a small hitch with my car.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a seed/pip' — a tiny seed represents a small, annoying snag or problem that gets in the way.

fr: tirer les vers du nez à quelqu'un
en: to worm information out of someone
lemma: tirer les vers du nez à quelqu'un
ipa: /ti.ʁe le vɛʁ dy ne a kɛl.kœ̃/
exampleFr: Elle a fini par lui tirer les vers du nez et il a tout avoué.
exampleEn: She finally wormed the truth out of him and he confessed everything.
mnemonic: Literally 'to pull worms from someone's nose' — a grotesque image of extracting something hidden, meaning to skillfully extract secret information.
audioText: tirer les vers du nez à quelqu'un

fr: avoir le cœur sur la main
en: to be extremely generous
lemma: avoir le cœur sur la main
exampleFr: Elle aide toujours tout le monde, elle a vraiment le cœur sur la main.
exampleEn: She always helps everyone, she's incredibly generous.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the heart on the hand' — the heart held out openly in the hand for all to see and take, symbolizing great generosity.
audioText: avoir le cœur sur la main

en: to have a green thumb
exampleFr: Toutes ses plantes sont magnifiques, elle a vraiment la main verte.
exampleEn: All her plants are beautiful, she really has a green thumb.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the green hand' — a hand seemingly tinted green by constant, skillful gardening, meaning a natural talent for growing plants.

fr: casser du sucre sur le dos de quelqu'un
en: to bad-mouth someone behind their back
lemma: casser du sucre sur le dos de quelqu'un
ipa: /ka.se dy sykʁ syʁ lə do də kɛl.kœ̃/
exampleFr: Arrêtez de casser du sucre sur son dos, il n'est pas là pour se défendre.
exampleEn: Stop bad-mouthing him behind his back, he's not here to defend himself.
mnemonic: Literally 'to break sugar on someone's back' — an old image of crushing sugar loaves on someone's back behind them, meaning to gossip maliciously about someone in their absence.
audioText: casser du sucre sur le dos de quelqu'un

en: to deceive, to con someone
exampleFr: Ce vendeur nous a roulés dans la farine avec sa fausse promotion.
exampleEn: That salesman conned us with his fake discount.
mnemonic: Literally 'to roll someone in flour' — like coating meat before frying to disguise it, this means covering someone in deception, tricking them.

en: to be knee-high to a grasshopper, very small or young
exampleFr: Je le connais depuis qu'il est haut comme trois pommes.
exampleEn: I've known him since he was knee-high to a grasshopper.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be as tall as three apples' — stacking three small apples gives a tiny height, describing a very small child.

fr: ne pas être dans son assiette
en: to not feel well, to be off
lemma: ne pas être dans son assiette
exampleFr: Tu es pâle, tu n'as pas l'air dans ton assiette aujourd'hui.
exampleEn: You're pale, you don't seem to be feeling well today.
mnemonic: Literally 'to not be in one's plate' — feeling out of place on your own plate captures the sense of feeling physically or emotionally off.
audioText: ne pas être dans son assiette

en: to have stage fright, to be nervous before a performance
exampleFr: Avant de monter sur scène, l'actrice avait le trac.
exampleEn: Before going on stage, the actress had stage fright.
mnemonic: 'Trac' itself means jittery nerves before a performance — 'avoir le trac' simply pairs it with 'avoir' to describe feeling that anxious flutter.

fr: se mettre le doigt dans l'œil
en: to be completely mistaken
lemma: se mettre le doigt dans l'œil
exampleFr: Si tu crois que je vais accepter, tu te mets le doigt dans l'œil.
exampleEn: If you think I'm going to accept, you're completely mistaken.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put one's finger in one's eye' — a painful, blind mistake, showing just how wrong someone's assumption really is.
audioText: se mettre le doigt dans l'œil

en: to do a pointless, wasted task
exampleFr: Ce stage ne m'apprend rien, j'ai l'impression de peigner la girafe toute la journée.
exampleEn: This internship isn't teaching me anything, I feel like I'm wasting my time all day.
mnemonic: Literally 'to comb the giraffe' — an absurd, useless task (who combs a giraffe?), representing pointless busywork.

en: to be a bit crazy, to have a screw loose
exampleFr: Il parle tout seul dans la rue, je crois qu'il a une araignée au plafond.
exampleEn: He talks to himself in the street, I think he's got a screw loose.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a spider on the ceiling' — a spider scuttling around inside one's head/ceiling suggests something is not quite right up there.

fr: courir sur le haricot à quelqu'un
en: to get on someone's nerves
lemma: courir sur le haricot à quelqu'un
exampleFr: Arrête, tu commences à me courir sur le haricot avec tes remarques.
exampleEn: Stop it, you're starting to get on my nerves with your comments.
mnemonic: Literally 'to run on someone's bean' — 'haricot' slangily refers to a toe here, so someone figuratively running over your toes is being extremely irritating.
audioText: courir sur le haricot à quelqu'un

fr: jeter de l'huile sur le feu
en: to add fuel to the fire
lemma: jeter de l'huile sur le feu
exampleFr: Ne dis rien de plus, tu ne fais que jeter de l'huile sur le feu.
exampleEn: Don't say anything more, you're just adding fuel to the fire.
mnemonic: Literally 'to throw oil on the fire' — oil makes flames roar higher, just as certain words or actions make an argument worse.
audioText: jeter de l'huile sur le feu

fr: être au four et au moulin
en: to be everywhere at once, juggling too many tasks
lemma: être au four et au moulin
exampleFr: Avec trois enfants et deux emplois, elle est toujours au four et au moulin.
exampleEn: With three kids and two jobs, she's always juggling everything at once.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be at the oven and at the mill' — trying to be in two distant workplaces simultaneously, meaning to be overstretched doing many things at once.
audioText: être au four et au moulin

fr: avoir les yeux plus gros que le ventre
en: to bite off more than one can chew, eyes bigger than stomach
lemma: avoir les yeux plus gros que le ventre
ipa: /a.vwaʁ le zjø ply gʁo kə lə vɑ̃tʁ/
exampleFr: Il a pris trois desserts et n'a rien fini : il a les yeux plus gros que le ventre.
exampleEn: He took three desserts and didn't finish any: his eyes were bigger than his stomach.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have eyes bigger than the stomach' — wanting, with the eyes, more food or more of something than you can actually handle.
audioText: avoir les yeux plus gros que le ventre

fr: mettre tous ses œufs dans le même panier
en: to put all one's eggs in one basket
lemma: mettre tous ses œufs dans le même panier
ipa: /mɛtʁ tu se zø dɑ̃ lə mɛm pa.nje/
exampleFr: Investir toutes tes économies dans une seule entreprise, c'est mettre tous tes œufs dans le même panier.
exampleEn: Investing all your savings in a single company is putting all your eggs in one basket.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put all one's eggs in the same basket' — if the basket falls, every egg breaks at once, meaning to risk everything on one single option.
audioText: mettre tous ses œufs dans le même panier

fr: avoir du pain sur la planche
en: to have a lot of work to do
lemma: avoir du pain sur la planche
exampleFr: Avec ce nouveau projet, on a du pain sur la planche pour les prochains mois.
exampleEn: With this new project, we have a lot of work ahead of us for the next few months.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have bread on the board' — dough still waiting on the board to be shaped and baked represents a large amount of work still to be done.
audioText: avoir du pain sur la planche

fr: ne pas y aller par quatre chemins
en: to get straight to the point
lemma: ne pas y aller par quatre chemins
ipa: /nə pa zi a.le paʁ katʁ ʃə.mɛ̃/
exampleFr: Je ne vais pas y aller par quatre chemins : ce projet est annulé.
exampleEn: I'll get straight to the point: this project is cancelled.
mnemonic: Literally 'to not go there by four paths' — taking the one direct route instead of four winding ones means speaking directly, without detours.
audioText: ne pas y aller par quatre chemins

en: to be utterly astonished
exampleFr: Quand elle a appris la nouvelle, elle est tombée des nues.
exampleEn: When she heard the news, she was completely stunned.
mnemonic: Literally 'to fall from the clouds' — dropping suddenly out of the sky captures the shock of learning something totally unexpected.

en: to have good instincts, to be shrewd
exampleFr: En vendant ses actions avant la crise, il a eu le nez creux.
exampleEn: By selling his shares before the crash, he showed great instinct.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a hollow nose' — a nose with extra room to sniff things out represents an unusually sharp instinct for sensing what's coming.

en: to worry oneself sick
exampleFr: Ne te fais pas des cheveux blancs pour cet examen, tu es bien préparé.
exampleEn: Don't worry yourself sick over this exam, you're well prepared.
mnemonic: Literally 'to make oneself white hair' — worry is imagined as aging you so fast your hair turns grey or white.

en: to be completely broke
exampleFr: Je ne peux pas sortir ce week-end, je suis fauché comme les blés.
exampleEn: I can't go out this weekend, I'm totally broke.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be mown down like the wheat' — a wheat field cut flush to the ground has nothing left standing, just like an empty wallet.

en: to feel blue, to be down
exampleFr: Depuis qu'il a raté son examen, il a le bourdon.
exampleEn: Ever since he failed his exam, he's been feeling down.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the bumblebee' — a buzzing, droning bee in your head suggests a heavy, gloomy mood weighing you down.

en: to pull an all-nighter
exampleFr: J'ai passé une nuit blanche pour finir ce rapport.
exampleEn: I pulled an all-nighter to finish this report.
mnemonic: Literally 'to spend a white night' — a night left 'blank,' with no sleep filling it in, meaning to stay awake the whole night.

en: to arouse suspicion, to give a hint
exampleFr: Son silence soudain m'a mis la puce à l'oreille.
exampleEn: His sudden silence made me suspicious.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put the flea in the ear' — a tiny, itchy flea near the ear keeps nagging at you, just like a nagging suspicion that something is off.

en: to worry oneself sick, to fret intensely
exampleFr: Elle s'est fait un sang d'encre en attendant les résultats de son fils.
exampleEn: She was worried sick waiting for her son's results.
mnemonic: Literally 'to make oneself blood of ink' — imagining your blood turning as thick and dark as ink conveys extreme anxiety and worry.

en: to have the gift of gab, to be very talkative
exampleFr: Ma nièce a la langue bien pendue, elle parle sans arrêt.
exampleEn: My niece has quite the gift of gab, she never stops talking.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a well-hung tongue' — a tongue that swings freely and easily describes someone who talks fluently and non-stop.

en: to bite the dust, to be defeated
exampleFr: L'équipe favorite a mordu la poussière face à des débutants.
exampleEn: The favorite team bit the dust against a bunch of beginners.
mnemonic: Literally 'to bite the dust' — falling face-first to the ground in defeat, exactly as in the English equivalent.

fr: avoir des fourmis dans les jambes
en: to have pins and needles, restless legs
lemma: avoir des fourmis dans les jambes
exampleFr: Après deux heures assis dans le train, j'ai des fourmis dans les jambes.
exampleEn: After two hours sitting on the train, I've got pins and needles in my legs.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have ants in the legs' — the tingling sensation of numb legs feels like tiny ants crawling underneath the skin.
audioText: avoir des fourmis dans les jambes

en: to be completely innocent
exampleFr: Malgré les accusations, il est blanc comme neige dans cette affaire.
exampleEn: Despite the accusations, he is completely innocent in this matter.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be white as snow' — pure, untouched snow with no stains represents someone free of any guilt or wrongdoing.

fr: avoir maille à partir avec quelqu'un
en: to have a dispute with someone, to be at odds
lemma: avoir maille à partir avec quelqu'un
exampleFr: Il a eu maille à partir avec son voisin à cause du bruit.
exampleEn: He had a dispute with his neighbor because of the noise.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a small coin to split with someone' — an old coin too small to divide fairly led to quarrels, hence 'having issues' with someone today.
audioText: avoir maille à partir avec quelqu'un

en: to move heaven and earth
exampleFr: Ses parents ont remué ciel et terre pour financer ses études.
exampleEn: His parents moved heaven and earth to fund his studies.
mnemonic: Literally 'to stir up sky and earth' — mobilizing the entire universe to achieve something shows the extraordinary effort being made.

en: to be green with envy
exampleFr: Quand il a vu ma nouvelle voiture, il était vert de jalousie.
exampleEn: When he saw my new car, he was green with envy.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be green with jealousy' — the same vivid color association as in English, where envy is pictured as a sickly green tint.

en: to have the last word
exampleFr: Dans cette famille, c'est toujours grand-mère qui a le dernier mot.
exampleEn: In this family, grandma always has the last word.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the last word' — the same direct meaning as in English: to win an argument by speaking the final, decisive statement.

en: to turn a deaf ear, to ignore deliberately
exampleFr: Il fait la sourde oreille à toutes nos demandes.
exampleEn: He turns a deaf ear to all our requests.
mnemonic: Literally 'to make the deaf ear' — pretending to have a deaf ear so as not to hear something you'd rather ignore.

en: to force a laugh, to laugh nervously or insincerely
exampleFr: Il a ri jaune quand on a évoqué son erreur devant tout le monde.
exampleEn: He gave a forced laugh when his mistake was mentioned in front of everyone.
mnemonic: Literally 'to laugh yellow' — yellow, an unhealthy-looking color, tints the laugh to show it's fake or uncomfortable rather than genuine.

en: to be on pins and needles, very anxious
exampleFr: En attendant les résultats médicaux, elle était sur des charbons ardents.
exampleEn: While waiting for the medical results, she was on pins and needles.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be on burning coals' — standing on hot coals would make anyone fidget anxiously, mirroring intense nervous anticipation.

en: to hog the credit, to take more than one's share
exampleFr: Dans ce projet de groupe, il essaie toujours de tirer la couverture à lui.
exampleEn: In this group project, he always tries to take all the credit for himself.
mnemonic: Literally 'to pull the blanket to oneself' — like yanking a shared blanket to cover only yourself, leaving others out in the cold.

fr: avoir la tête sur les épaules
en: to be sensible, level-headed
lemma: avoir la tête sur les épaules
exampleFr: Malgré son jeune âge, elle a la tête sur les épaules.
exampleEn: Despite her young age, she's very level-headed.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have one's head on one's shoulders' — a head properly and firmly in place, unlike someone whose head is 'in the clouds,' shows good sense.
audioText: avoir la tête sur les épaules

fr: jeter un pavé dans la mare
en: to stir up controversy, to drop a bombshell
lemma: jeter un pavé dans la mare
exampleFr: Sa déclaration a jeté un pavé dans la mare au sein du parti.
exampleEn: His statement stirred up a huge controversy within the party.
mnemonic: Literally 'to throw a paving stone into the pond' — the splash disturbs everything calm around it, like a shocking statement disrupting the peace.
audioText: jeter un pavé dans la mare

en: to jump from one topic to another
exampleFr: Pendant la réunion, il n'arrêtait pas de passer du coq à l'âne.
exampleEn: During the meeting, he kept jumping from one unrelated topic to another.
mnemonic: Literally 'to go from the rooster to the donkey' — two completely unrelated barnyard animals side by side capture an abrupt, illogical change of subject.

en: to have a say in the matter
exampleFr: En tant qu'actionnaire, elle a voix au chapitre dans les décisions de l'entreprise.
exampleEn: As a shareholder, she has a say in the company's decisions.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a voice at the chapter' — from monks with a vote at chapter meetings, it now means having the right to give one's opinion on a decision.

fr: mettre la clé sous la porte
en: to shut down, to close up shop
lemma: mettre la clé sous la porte
exampleFr: Faute de clients, le petit magasin a dû mettre la clé sous la porte.
exampleEn: For lack of customers, the small shop had to shut down.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put the key under the door' — leaving the key behind as you close up for good, meaning a business has permanently shut down.
audioText: mettre la clé sous la porte

fr: être sur la même longueur d'onde
en: to be on the same wavelength
lemma: être sur la même longueur d'onde
exampleFr: Avec mon associé, on est toujours sur la même longueur d'onde.
exampleEn: My business partner and I are always on the same wavelength.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be on the same wavelength' — like two radios tuned to the same frequency, meaning to think alike and understand each other easily.
audioText: être sur la même longueur d'onde

fr: ne pas avoir la langue dans sa poche
en: to not be shy about speaking one's mind
lemma: ne pas avoir la langue dans sa poche
ipa: /nə pa za.vwaʁ la lɑ̃g dɑ̃ sa pɔʃ/
exampleFr: Demande-lui son avis, elle n'a pas la langue dans sa poche.
exampleEn: Ask her for her opinion, she's never shy about speaking her mind.
mnemonic: Literally 'to not have one's tongue in one's pocket' — the tongue is out and ready, not tucked away, meaning someone speaks up freely and readily.
audioText: ne pas avoir la langue dans sa poche

en: to tighten one's belt, to cut expenses
exampleFr: Avec la hausse des prix, on doit se serrer la ceinture ce mois-ci.
exampleEn: With rising prices, we have to tighten our belts this month.
mnemonic: Literally 'to tighten the belt' — eating less makes a belt loose, so cinching it tighter symbolizes cutting back on spending.

en: to let bygones be bygones, to forgive
exampleFr: Je préfère passer l'éponge sur cette dispute et repartir sur de bonnes bases.
exampleEn: I'd rather let this argument go and start fresh.
mnemonic: Literally 'to pass the sponge' — wiping a chalkboard clean with a sponge erases what happened, meaning to forgive and forget a past wrong.

fr: prendre le taureau par les cornes
en: to take the bull by the horns
lemma: prendre le taureau par les cornes
exampleFr: Au lieu de fuir le problème, il a décidé de prendre le taureau par les cornes.
exampleEn: Instead of avoiding the problem, he decided to take the bull by the horns.
mnemonic: Literally 'to take the bull by the horns' — the same bold image as in English: confronting a difficult situation head-on and decisively.
audioText: prendre le taureau par les cornes

en: to feel sad, heavy-hearted
exampleFr: Elle avait le cœur gros en quittant sa ville natale.
exampleEn: She felt heavy-hearted leaving her hometown.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have a big heart' — here the heart is swollen not with generosity but with sadness, weighed down and heavy with sorrow.

fr: mettre les points sur les i
en: to spell things out clearly, dot the i's
lemma: mettre les points sur les i
exampleFr: Avant de signer, je veux mettre les points sur les i concernant nos responsabilités.
exampleEn: Before signing, I want to spell out our responsibilities clearly.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put the dots on the i's' — finishing every letter completely and precisely, leaving nothing ambiguous or unclear.
audioText: mettre les points sur les i

en: to turn the page, to move on
exampleFr: Après leur rupture, elle a décidé de tourner la page.
exampleEn: After their breakup, she decided to turn the page and move on.
mnemonic: Literally 'to turn the page' — just as in English, closing one chapter of a book to start reading the next represents moving forward from the past.

en: to be in bad shape, heading down a bad path
exampleFr: Depuis qu'il traîne avec cette bande, il file un mauvais coton.
exampleEn: Ever since he started hanging out with that crowd, he's been heading down a bad path.
mnemonic: Literally 'to spin bad cotton' — a weaver producing poor-quality thread signals something is going wrong, whether health or behavior.

en: to get to the bottom of something, to find out for sure
exampleFr: Je vais l'appeler pour en avoir le cœur net.
exampleEn: I'm going to call him to get to the bottom of it.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the heart clear about it' — clearing all doubt from the heart means settling an uncertainty once and for all.

en: to sulk, to give someone the silent treatment
exampleFr: Depuis notre dispute, mon frère me fait la tête.
exampleEn: Ever since our argument, my brother has been giving me the silent treatment.
mnemonic: Literally 'to make the head' — pulling a sour, pouting face is the visible sign of sulking and refusing to speak to someone.

en: to have charisma, sex appeal
exampleFr: Cette actrice a du chien, elle attire tous les regards.
exampleEn: That actress has real charisma, she catches everyone's eye.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have some dog' — a lively, spirited dog's energy is compared to a person's magnetic charm and allure.

fr: mettre quelqu'un au pied du mur
en: to force someone to face facts, to corner them into deciding
lemma: mettre quelqu'un au pied du mur
exampleFr: Ses collègues l'ont mis au pied du mur en exigeant une réponse immédiate.
exampleEn: His colleagues cornered him by demanding an immediate answer.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put someone at the foot of the wall' — with a wall right behind them and nowhere left to retreat, they must finally decide or act.
audioText: mettre quelqu'un au pied du mur

en: to make a big deal out of nothing
exampleFr: C'est juste une petite erreur, ne fais pas tout un fromage !
exampleEn: It's just a small mistake, don't make a huge deal out of it!
mnemonic: Literally 'to make a whole cheese out of it' — turning a small, plain bit of milk into an enormous cheese mirrors blowing a minor issue way out of proportion.

en: to be really stupid
exampleFr: Il a encore oublié ses clés, il est bête comme ses pieds parfois.
exampleEn: He forgot his keys again, he can be really dumb sometimes.
mnemonic: Literally 'to be as stupid as one's feet' — feet obviously can't think at all, so comparing someone's intelligence to feet is a playful insult.

en: to be scared, to have the jitters
exampleFr: Avant l'entretien, j'avoue que j'avais les jetons.
exampleEn: Before the interview, I admit I had the jitters.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have the tokens/chips' — like a gambler nervously clutching casino chips, it means being nervous or scared.

en: to get rejected romantically
exampleFr: Il lui a demandé de sortir avec lui et s'est pris un râteau.
exampleEn: He asked her out and got rejected.
mnemonic: Literally 'to take a rake (in the face)' — like stepping on a garden rake that snaps up and hits you, this describes the sting of being turned down.

fr: avoir des atomes crochus avec quelqu'un
en: to click with someone, to hit it off
lemma: avoir des atomes crochus avec quelqu'un
exampleFr: Dès notre première rencontre, on a eu des atomes crochus.
exampleEn: From our very first meeting, we really clicked.
mnemonic: Literally 'to have hooked atoms with someone' — imagining tiny atoms that latch onto each other like hooks captures an instant, natural connection between two people.
audioText: avoir des atomes crochus avec quelqu'un

fr: mettre de l'eau dans son vin
en: to tone down one's demands, to compromise
lemma: mettre de l'eau dans son vin
exampleFr: Pour trouver un accord, chacun devra mettre de l'eau dans son vin.
exampleEn: To reach an agreement, everyone will have to make some compromises.
mnemonic: Literally 'to put water in one's wine' — diluting strong wine softens it, just as softening one's strong demands leads to compromise.
audioText: mettre de l'eau dans son vin

en: to rack one's brain
exampleFr: J'ai eu beau me creuser la tête, je n'ai pas trouvé la solution.
exampleEn: No matter how much I racked my brain, I couldn't find the solution.
mnemonic: Literally 'to dig a hole in one's head' — digging deep into your own mind captures the intense mental effort of trying hard to think or remember.

en: to play with fire
exampleFr: En cachant la vérité à son patron, il joue avec le feu.
exampleEn: By hiding the truth from his boss, he's playing with fire.
mnemonic: Literally 'to play with fire' — the same vivid warning as in English: taking a reckless risk that could easily backfire and cause harm.

en: to be scared
exampleFr: J'avoue que j'ai la frousse avant chaque examen oral.
exampleEn: I admit I get scared before every oral exam.
mnemonic: 'Frousse' is a slang word for intense fear itself — 'avoir la frousse' simply means to feel that gripping fright.

en: to lose one's mind, to go crazy
exampleFr: Avec tout ce stress au travail, je crois que je vais perdre la boule.
exampleEn: With all this stress at work, I think I'm going to lose my mind.
mnemonic: Literally 'to lose the ball' — 'boule' slangily refers to the head or mind, so 'losing' it means losing your sanity or ability to think straight.
